_about: Budgets are ratios against a yardstick measured in the same run and beside the layer it divides -- dictionary, integer and string work in a loop, never this project's code -- because seconds recorded on one machine cannot gate another, and a yardstick written in C would barely notice which interpreter called it while this project is Python all the way down. The yardstick is measured again in every pass, next to the layer, because measuring it once at the start cancels steady load out and amplifies load that lands on one window and not the other: at the old sequence, bursts timed onto the yardstick alone drove the reported ratio to 0.41x and onto the layers alone to 1.33x, on one idle machine with one unchanged tree, and a loaded machine turned an unchanged tree red twice in twenty-four runs. Passes continue past the first three while they disagree by more than a quarter, because under load the fastest of three can still be a pass where only one of the two numbers got a clean window. One entry per operating system, because the ratio does not travel between them either; a platform with no entry passes and says so, since there is no way to write a budget for a machine before a run on it -- but `platforms_expected` lists the keys that already have one, because a platform loses its budget by being renamed as easily as by being deleted and both look like silence. Adding a platform means adding it in both places, which is the point: one of them is the claim and the other is the figure. The seconds below are for a reader and are also compared: a layer whose absolute time collapses has stopped doing its work, which no ratio can tell from a fast machine.

Darwin._from: one run on an idle machine, chosen as the closest to the mean of five. Re-recorded because the corpus grew from 61 inputs to 63: a File reference case on a pack outside 02004's family had no case here, so a change that gives that question to another pack reported as nothing moved. `corpus_pass` rose from 97.5 to 104 with the two inputs, which is the only layer the corpus is in; the other four moved 3-5% on the same tree and are drift, not a change -- recorded together because the tool measures them in one pass and a mixed file would not say when each half was taken. Those five spanned cold_start 58.8-61.1 (4% peak to peak), corpus_pass 102-106 (4%), scale 86.2-88.7 (3%), rules_layer 0.446-0.461 (3%), supplied_template 28.3-29.2 (3%). Peak-to-peak over a stated number of runs is the figure worth quoting; a standard deviation of three samples reads reassuringly and hides what a reader meets.
